objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of the new electrosurgical unit with a thermally conductive electrode tip and thermal management system in reducing thermal spread at the target zone compared to the current electrosurgical unit.
dependent_variables: Thermal spread at the target zone (mm)
baseline: Current electrosurgical unit with no thermal management system (average thermal spread: 5.2 mm)
procedure: Prepare porcine liver tissue models for the experiment.
Set up the new electrosurgical unit with the thermally conductive electrode tip and thermal management system.
Set the power density to 100 W/cm² and the target temperature to 60°C.
Monitor the temperature at the target zone using the temperature sensor.
Adjust the power density accordingly using the thermal management system.
Measure the thermal spread at the target zone after 10 minutes of treatment.
expected_result: A 30% decrease in thermal spread at the target zone compared to the baseline.
falsification_condition: If the thermal spread at the target zone increases by more than 10% compared to the baseline, or if the temperature at the target zone exceeds 70°C, indicating inadequate thermal management.
sample_requirements: 10 porcine liver tissue models, each with a diameter of 5 cm and a thickness of 1 cm.
safety_constraints: The experiment must be conducted in a well-ventilated area, and the electrosurgical unit must be operated by a trained professional.
estimated_cost: $10,000 (including the cost of the new electrosurgical unit, porcine liver tissue models, and personnel)
estimated_duration: 6 weeks (including preparation, data collection, and analysis)
information_gain: The experiment will provide valuable information on the effectiveness of the new electrosurgical unit in reducing thermal spread at the target zone, which can be used to improve the design and functionality of the device.
